comment: The README on the maker's repository describes the module the code does not build. It lists a DATA input for the source voltage to be sampled and shifted; there is no DATA input, and the bit shifted in is the register's own last bit exclusive-ORed with a random flip. It calls the third jack an INJECT CV; the jack is PROB_CV_IN, configInput names it "Probability CV" and the panel prints PROB CV. It says DENS "controls the intensity and value range of the injected glitch data"; DENS is read at one place only, as the probability that an accent pulse is fired alongside a gate. It says the GATE output fires whenever a mutation or a manual injection occurs; the gate actually fires whenever the bit that has just rolled round is set, whether or not it was mutated. The panel carries two sets of output labels drawn 1.5mm apart: res/IdmGlitchNode.svg prints GATE, PITCH and ACCENT at x 20.64, 40.64 and 60.64mm while the jacks are at 32.64, 48.64 and 64.64mm, and a runtime text widget prints INJ, GATE, PITCH and ACC correctly aligned beneath them. The SVG row is the misaligned one. The register starts at 0x5A5A and RST_IN restores that same value, so a reset does not clear it. The screen is a single TransparentWidget with no ParamWidget inside it, so nothing on it is clickable. The two lights are set from the gate and accent voltages, so they follow those jacks exactly.
